item.title: Seeing page comment replies: Re: Seeing page comment replies
item.content:encoded: Wikidot doesn't have any automated notifications. Closest you could get is maybe setting up an RSS feed, or just checking the discussion threads manually via the list on your wikidot profile.

item.title: Weird Question: Re: Weird Question
item.content:encoded:
Personally I feel like D-Class that are fleshed out as characters with backgrounds, unique or ongoing skills, and personalities often improve SCPs, especially if there's a lot of interaction with them in logs. Also especially if they survive through multiple SCPs. SCP-2515 and SCP-4479 are great examples. D-11424 even has their own tag.

I mean, from a document "realism" standpoint, they wouldn't mention background unless it was relevant to the testing (like in 2515), but 1) "realism" is highly overrated and 2) it can still come up in natural conversation.

item.title: Weird Question: Re: Weird Question
item.content:encoded:
You mind telling me the name of that tale

I think it's Ethics. I believe the author, fieldstone, has some other tales about the Foundation being cast as a morally-gray organization.

I was thinking about putting some exploration logs in my article

I'm not sure the in-universe Foundation would find it pertinent to identify D-Class backgrounds for exploration logs, unless said backgrounds would make a difference in the testing protocol (a D-Class who is a former professional spelunker going into a cave-based anomaly, for example, compared to a D-Class with no experience whatsoever for the type of terrain being explored).

I thought that it would be necessary to add a little background information about the D-Class so that the readers can warm up to the character.

Unless that background info makes sense from the perspective of a researcher, don't include it. Remember, the in-universe Foundation has no need to make readers of a dry professional report "warm up" to individuals mentioned in logs. If you include character information, there needs to be a good reason in-universe for a researcher to have it.

item.title: I feel as if a lot of stuff is missing.: Junior Staff Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
bite_this_onions, please note that this forum is for general inquiries and assistance, not for soliciting critique. All crit requests and activities related to critique/feedback therein should be done either in our Draft Critique Forum or Ideas Critique Forum.

However, per the New Draft Forum Policy, all first-time authors must have received two greenlights on a concept thread in the latter forum prior to being able to post in the former. If you plan on using these resources, please take the time to go through all of the Required Reading before posting to ensure that the contents of your thread(s) adhere to the guidelines of the forum(s) in question.

Additionally, also take note of the other available resources for critique made available including contacting a member of the Butterfly Squad or heading over to the #thecritters chatroom on our IRC network (SkipIRC).

If you have any other questions or concerns, please feel free to reach out to myself or another member of SCP Wiki Staff.

item.title: Where would I publish work about regular human characters?: Re: Where would I publish work about regular human characters?
item.content:encoded:
I want to know if there's a place for this or if this is to be kept solely in the tales and not have a description page

If you're looking to just have an overview of laundry-list information and statistics pertaining to recurring character, the closest the site has is a series hub page. For example, the Kiryu Labs Hub.

That said, if you want to have a hub page, you need to have tales to populate the hub first.

item.title: Do tales need to be greenlit if they are your first article?: Re: Do tales need to be greenlit if they are your first article?
item.content:encoded: In the strictest of terms you don't need to be greenlit to post anything. However, greenlights allow you to use the Feedback and Critique Forum which you will probably want to use because it's the easiest place to get crit on your article. Tales, just like SCPs and GoI Formats, require two greenlights before being posted to the Feedback and Critique Forum.

item.title: SCP Radio saves handlers for feet pics: Re: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
I didn't say I wasn't looking for concept critique

If you want critique on a concept, please follow the template noted in the Ideas Critique forum required reading, and do not provide a sandbox draft unless a reviewer asks to read a full draft.

If you're expecting reviewers to read your sandbox draft before providing critique, you can ask for draft feedback in the IRC chatrooms. Greenlights are not required there, though some reviewers may still ask authors to first go through the greenlighting process if the core concept needs revision before the draft itself can be fixed.
